54060-beyond-the-gates.title: Beyond The Gates.
54060-beyond-the-gates.creator: Unknown
54060-beyond-the-gates.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. I hoped a not altogether valueless, middle age. I had used life and loved it. Beyond the idle impulse of a weary moment, which signifies no more than the reflex action of a mental muscle, and which I had been in the habit of rating accordingly, I had never wished to die. I was well, vigorous, and active.

arxiv-2011-08585.title: Splitting Schemes for Some Second-Order Evolution Equations Journal: arXiv
arxiv-2011-08585.creator: Petr N. Vabishchevich
arxiv-2011-08585.description: Abstract We consider the Cauchy problem for a second-order evolution equation, in which the problem operator is the sum of two self-adjoint operators. The main feature of the problem is that one of the operators is represented in the form of the product of operator A A by its conjugate A ∗ A^{*} .

arxiv-2106-08759.title: OpenSSLNTRU: Faster post-quantum TLS key exchange
arxiv-2106-08759.creator: Daniel J. Bernstein 1,2 , Billy Bob Brumley 3 , Ming-Shing Chen 2 , and Nicola Tuveri 3
arxiv-2106-08759.description: Abstract Google’s CECPQ1 experiment in 2016 integrated a post-quantum key-exchange algorithm, newhope1024 , into TLS 1.2. The Google-Cloudflare CECPQ2 experiment in 2019 integrated a more efficient key-exchange algorithm, ntruhrss701 , into TLS 1.3. This paper revisits the choices made in CECPQ2, and shows how to achieve higher performance for post-quantum key exchange in TLS 1.

arxiv-2108-10428.title: Coherent energy loss effects in dihadron azimuthal angular correlations in Deep Inelastic Scattering at small x x
arxiv-2108-10428.creator: Filip Bergabo, Jamal Jalilian-Marian
arxiv-2108-10428.description: Abstract We perform an exploratory study of the role of coherent, medium-induced energy loss in azimuthal angular correlations in dihadron production in Deep Inelastic Scattering (DIS) at small x x where the target proton/nucleus is modeled as a Color Glass Condensate.

arxiv-2109-15307.title: Enforced symmetry breaking by invertible topological order
arxiv-2109-15307.creator: Shang-Qiang Ning, Yang Qi, Zheng-Cheng Gu, Chenjie Wang
arxiv-2109-15307.description: Abstract It is well known that two-dimensional fermionic systems with a nonzero Chern number must break the time reversal symmetry, manifested by the appearance of chiral edge modes on an open boundary. Such an incompatibility between topology and symmetry can occur more generally. We will refer to this phenomenon as enforced symmetry breaking (ESB) by topological orders.

arxiv-2209-11995.title: Time-dependent properties of run-and-tumble particles: Density relaxation
arxiv-2209-11995.creator: Tanmoy Chakraborty, Punyabrata Pradhan
arxiv-2209-11995.description: Abstract We characterize collective diffusion of hardcore run-and-tumble particles (RTPs) by explicitly calculating the bulk-diffusion coefficient D ⁡ ( ρ , γ ) D(\rho,\gamma) for arbitrary density ρ \rho and tumbling rate γ \gamma , in systems on a d d dimensional periodic lattice.

arxiv-2310-18681.title: DySurv: Dynamic Deep Learning Model for Survival Analysis with Conditional Variational Inference
arxiv-2310-18681.creator: Munib Mesinovic, MSc, Peter Watkinson, PhD, Tingting Zhu, PhD
arxiv-2310-18681.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Munib Mesinovic, MSc, Peter Watkinson, PhD, Tingting Zhu, PhD. Objective: Machine learning applications for longitudinal electronic health records often forecast the risk of events at fixed time points whereas survival analysis achieves dynamic risk prediction by estimating time-to-event distributions. Here, we propose a novel conditional variational autoencoder-based method, DySurv, which uses a combination of static and longitudinal measurements from electronic health records to estimate the individual risk of death dynamically.

arxiv-2405-04933.title: On Coordinate Frames in Axisymmetric Static Vacuum Spacetimes and Implications for Observations
arxiv-2405-04933.creator: A. Seifert
arxiv-2405-04933.description: Abstract While a physical theory should be independent of the coordinate frame chosen by any observer, the observations themselves in fact depend on the choice of coordinates. In particular, different coordinate frames reflect different symmetries seen by a local observer.

arxiv-2408-16140.title: SoK: Identifying Limitations and Bridging Gaps of Cybersecurity Capability Maturity Models (CCMMs)
arxiv-2408-16140.creator: Lasini Liyanage, Nalin Asanka Gamagedara Arachchilage, Giovanni Russello
arxiv-2408-16140.description: Abstract . In the rapidly evolving digital landscape, where organisations are increasingly vulnerable to cybersecurity threats, Cybersecurity Capability Maturity Models (CCMMs) emerge as pivotal tools in enhancing organisational cybersecurity posture. CCMMs provide a structured framework to guide organisations in assessing their current cybersecurity capabilities, identifying critical gaps, and prioritising improvements.

arxiv-2507-02525.title: Data-Driven Transient Growth Analysis
arxiv-2507-02525.creator: Zhicheng Kai, Peter Frame, Aaron Towne
arxiv-2507-02525.description: Abstract The transient growth of disturbances made possible by the non-normality of the linearized Navier-Stokes equations plays an important role in bypass transition for many shear flows. Transient growth is typically quantified by the maximum energy growth among all possible initial disturbances, which is given by the largest squared singular value of the matrix exponential of the linearized Navier-Stokes operator.

arxiv-2510-14867.title: Disorder-assisted Spin-Filtering at Metal/Ferromagnet Interfaces: An Alternative Route to Anisotropic Magnetoresistance
arxiv-2510-14867.creator: Ivan Iorsh, Mikhail Titov
arxiv-2510-14867.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ivan Iorsh, Mikhail Titov. We introduce a minimal interface-scattering mechanism that produces a sizable anisotropic magnetoresistance (AMR) in metal/ferromagnet bilayers (e.g., Pt/YIG) without invoking bulk spin or orbital Hall currents. In a δ \delta -layer model with interfacial exchange and Rashba spin-orbit coupling, charge transfer at a high-quality interface creates a spin-selective phase condition (interfacial spin filtering) that suppresses backscattering for one spin projection while enhancing momentum relaxation for the other.

arxiv-2601-13096.creator: Muhayy Ud Din, Waseem Akram, Ahsan B. Bakht, Irfan Hussain
arxiv-2601-13096.description: Abstract Maritime port inspection plays a critical role in ensuring safety, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency in complex maritime environments. However, existing inspection methods often rely on manual operations and conventional computer vision techniques that lack scalability and contextual understanding.

openalex-w3099237227.creator: Adriane Esquivel‐Muelbert, Oliver Lawrence Phillips, Roel Brienen, Sophie Fauset, Martin J. P. Sullivan, Timothy R. Baker, Kuo‐Jung Chao, Ted R. Feldpausch, Emanuel U. Gloor, Níro Higuchi, Jeanine J. Houwing‐Duistermaat, Jon Lloyd
openalex-w3099237227.description: The carbon sink capacity of tropical forests is substantially affected by tree mortality. However, the main drivers of tropical tree death remain largely unknown. Here we present a pan-Amazonian assessment of how and why trees die, analysing over 120,000 trees representing >...

plos-pone-0005320.creator: Lucas A. Mongiat, M. Soledad Espósito, Gabriela Lombardi et al.
plos-pone-0005320.description: PLOS ONE research article. Neurons born in the adult dentate gyrus develop, mature, and connect over a long interval that can last from six to eight weeks. It has been proposed that, during this period, developing neurons play a relevant role in hippocampal signal processing owing to their distinctive elec

pmc-10648075.title: Public Mixed Funding for Residential Aged Care Facilities Residents’ Needs in the Asia–Pacific Region: A Scoping Review
pmc-10648075.creator: David Lim, Ashley Grady, Karen P Y Liu, Ilaria Tocco Tussardi
pmc-10648075.description: Due to population aging and sociodemographic change, there is an increasing reliance on residential aged care facilities in the Asia–Pacific region. Most countries have adopted taxation as the primary means to levy capital for funding universal health services and means-testing of benefits may be further incorporated as a policy balance between horizontal equity and fiscal sustainability.

pmc-11357226.title: Modeling and Optimization of Ellagic Acid from Chebulae Fructus Using Response Surface Methodology Coupled with Artificial Neural Network
pmc-11357226.creator: Junkai Wu, Fan Yang, Liyang Guo, Zunlai Sheng
pmc-11357226.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The dried ripe fruit of Terminalia chebula Retz. is a common Chinese materia medica, and ellagic acid (EA), isolated from the plant, is an important bioactive component for medicinal purposes. This study aimed to delineate the optimal extraction parameters for extracting the EA content from Chebulae Fructus (CF), focusing on the variables of ethanol concentration, extraction temperature, liquid–solid ratio, and extraction time.

pmc-11447932.title: Hyperspectral imaging for pest symptom detection in bell pepper
pmc-11447932.creator: Marvin Krüger, Thomas Zemanek, Dominik Wuttke, Maximilian Dinkel, Albrecht Serfling, Elias Böckmann
pmc-11447932.description: BackgroundThe automation of pest monitoring is highly important for enhancing integrated pest management in practice. In this context, advanced technologies are becoming increasingly explored. Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) is a technique that has been used frequently in recent years in the context of natural science, and the successful detection of several fungal diseases and some pests has been reported.

pmc-11481439.title: Identification of novel proteins in inflammatory bowel disease based on the gut-brain axis: a multi-omics integrated analysis
pmc-11481439.creator: Yifeng Xu, Zhaoqi Yan, Liangji Liu
pmc-11481439.description: BackgroundThe gut-brain axis has garnered increasing attention, with observational studies suggesting its involvement in the disease activity and progression of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), but the precise mechanisms remain unclear.Materials and methodsIn this study, we aimed to investigate “novel proteins” underlying IBD in the brain using a comprehensive multi-omics analysis approach.

pmc-11533536.title: Enhanced surface functionalization of 2D molybdenum/tin chalcogenide nanostructures for effective SERS detection of Escherichia coli†
pmc-11533536.creator: Zainab Ishfaq, Layla A. Almutairi, M. Yasir Ali, Salhah Hamed Alrefaee, Mohamed Abdelsabour Fahmy, Elsammani Ali Shokralla, Lamiaa G. Alharbe, Adnan Ali, Arslan Ashfaq, A. R. Abd-Elwahed
pmc-11533536.description: Surface Enhanced Raman Spectroscopy (SERS) is a highly sensitive analytical technique used for fingerprint recognition of molecular samples. The SERS effect, which enhances Raman scattering signals, has been the subject of extensive research over the past few decades. More recently, the commercialization of portable Raman spectrometers has brought SERS closer to real-world applications.

pmc-11662445.title: Characterization of the Calmodulin-Like Protein Family in Chara braunii and their Conserved Interaction with the Calmodulin-Binding Transcription Activator Family
pmc-11662445.creator: Kyle Symonds, Udo Wali, Liam Duff, Wayne A Snedden
pmc-11662445.description: Calcium sensor proteins play important roles by detecting changes in intracellular calcium and relaying that information onto downstream targets through protein–protein interaction. Very little is known about calcium sensors from plant species that predate land colonization and the evolution of embryophytes.

pmc-11726086.title: Early bacteremia following allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation without antibiotic prophylaxis: epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance
pmc-11726086.creator: Nour Ben Abdeljelil, Rihab Ouerghi, Insaf Ben Yaiche, Amine Ben Moussa, Yosra Chebbi, Tarek Ben Othman
pmc-11726086.description: ObjectiveBacteremia is a serious complication in patients undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. The aim of this study was to determine the frequency, epidemiological profile, and risk factors of bacteremia early after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.MethodsAn observational descriptive retrospective study was conducted in patients who received transplants between January 2016 and December 2021.

pmc-12538448.title: The impact of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) and the Heads of Medicines Agencies (HMA) to address shortages of human and veterinary medicines across Europe
pmc-12538448.creator: Inga Abed, Vanessa Bennett, Brendan Cuddy, Sandra Dang, Juan García Burgos, Domenico Di Giorgio, Maria Lamas, Momir Radulovic, Nuno Simões, Rui Santos Ivo, Hugues Malonne, Monica Dias
pmc-12538448.description: Shortages of medicines are a global public health challenge with a significant impact on patient care. While the issue is at the top of the agenda of EU policymakers, regulators and healthcare providers, shortages are a complex problem with many contributing factors requiring multifaceted solutions.

pmc-12653547.title: The Role of TLR2/TLR4 Receptors in Host Genetic Susceptibility to Recurrent Vulvovaginitis
pmc-12653547.creator: John Routsias, Chrysoula Verra, Aristotelis Tsiakalos, Athanasios Tsakris, Maria Mavrouli, David S Perlin
pmc-12653547.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Vulvovaginal candidiasis (VVC) is a prevalent vaginal infection predominantly attributed to Candida albicans. A considerable proportion of women experience more than three episodes of VVC annually, a condition referred to as recurrent vulvovaginal candidiasis (RVVC). It is estimated that RVVC affects more than 130 million women globally each year and has a substantial negative impact on their quality of life, resulting in physical discomfort, psychological distress, and social stigma.

pmc-12723330.title: Smartphone‐Assisted Wireless Ultrasensitive Nitrite Detection in Food Samples via Hierarchical MXene/NiCoMn‐LDH/Sulfide Heterostructure on Flexible Laser‐Induced Graphene Electrode
pmc-12723330.creator: Kugalur Shanmugam Ranjith, Ali Mohammadi, A T Ezhil Vilian, Yonghyeon Park, Ganji Seeta Rama Raju, Yun Suk Huh, Young‐Kyu Han
pmc-12723330.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Designing a smartphone in‐built, wireless, ultrasensitive hybrid heterostructure‐based sensor is challenging, but it is potentially crucial for achieving efficient electrochemical responses related to real‐time food safety monitoring. Herein, the pioneering design of a few‐layered MXene‐tagged NiCoMn‐layered double hydroxide (LDH)/amorphous sulfide (MXe/NiCoMn‐LDH/S) hollow spheres were fabricated and tagged onto a laser‐induced graphene (LIG) electrode for smartphone‐based electrochemical detection of nitrite (NO2 −).

pmc-13218095.title: Health system responsiveness and associated factors among outpatients in primary healthcare units in Southern Ethiopia: a facility-based cross-sectional study
pmc-13218095.creator: Habtamu Esubalew Bezie, Zeleke Hailemariam, Mustefa Glagn, Biniyam Demisse Andarge, Tsegazeab Ayele Meshesha, Edlework Wondmagegn Atlaw, Kidus Temesgen Worsa, Sayih Mehari Degualem, Habtamu Wondmagegn Atlaw
pmc-13218095.description: ObjectiveTo assess the level of health system responsiveness (HSR) and its associated factors among outpatients attending primary healthcare units (PHCU) in Arba Minch, South Ethiopia.DesignFacility-based cross-sectional study.SettingThree PHCUs (one primary hospital and two health centres) in Arba Minch town, Southern Ethiopia.ParticipantsA total of 379 outpatients aged 18 years and above were selected using a systematic random sampling.

pmc-13222999.title: Storage temperature and quality dynamics of sun-aged red date vinegar beverage
pmc-13222999.creator: Zeshan Ali, Zinanone Rosaire Brottier, Jameel M. Al-Khayri, Muhammad Azhar, Othman Al-Dossary, Sam Al-Dalali, Bader Alsubaie, Mustafa I. Almaghasla
pmc-13222999.description: IntroductionThis study investigates the formulation, processing stability, and storage behavior of a vinegar-based beverage derived from red date (Ziziphus jujuba Mill.) vinegar produced via controlled fermentation and traditional sun-aging. To improve flavor and reduce sourness, goji berry juice and honey were added to the final formulation.
